newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes weaker in line with NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes weaker in line with NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes firmed midday Friday, following higher levels set by NYMEX and spot West Texas Intermediate.
No deals were reported on Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude amid thin Friday dealing. ANS gained 45 cents in line with a 75-cent increase in NYMEX January crude and flat discounts.
A major producer kept their ANS offer at $1.65 under January WTI.
Recent Line 63 deals were done on a posting plus basis only, traders said, with premiums talked $0.95 to $1.05 in the thinly traded market.
Line 63 at a discount to WTI had not been seen in months, traders said, noting deals done in the posting plus market fell between $0.95 abd $1.05.
Traders said higher inventories and a $0.50 to $1.00 decrease in posted prices forced heavy crudes lower mid-week.
Discounts for Kern River heavy crude remained 10 cents under postings to even with postings, traders said.
